items.title: Section: Why Lower Realms Can Think About Higher Ones, But Not the Reverse

items.zh: 下地煩惱能緣上地煩惱及事，非上地惑能緣下地煩惱及事。如是煩惱展轉相緣，及下地惑能緣上地。於此處所餘決擇文，更不復現。復次，俱生薩迦耶見唯無記性，數現行故，非極損惱自他處故。若分別起薩迦耶見，由堅執故，與前相違。在欲界者，唯不善性。若在上地，奢摩他力所制持故，多白淨法所攝受故，成無記性。由染污故，體是隱沒。所餘煩惱，由此道理，隨應當知。
items.en: Afflictions belonging to a lower realm can take a higher realm's afflictions and phenomena as their object; a higher realm's afflictions cannot take a lower realm's afflictions and phenomena as their object. Next, innate self-view is purely neutral, since it operates constantly yet does not severely harm oneself or others. Intellectually-adopted self-view, being firmly grasped, differs from this — in the desire realm it is purely unwholesome. In the higher realms, restrained by the power of calm-abiding and surrounded by predominantly wholesome qualities, it becomes neutral, yet remains, because of its defiled nature, a concealed kind of neutrality. The remaining afflictions should be understood by this same principle, according to what applies.

items.title: Section: Three Conditions That Actually Send an Affliction to a Miserable Rebirth

items.zh: 欲界煩惱為諸惡行安足處故，多不善性。又不善者，具三因緣能往惡趣，餘則不定。何等為三？謂極多修習，殷重、無間計為功德，不見其失，不見其患，縱情而起，是初因緣。用此煩惱以為依處，由身語意，於諸惡行作及增長，是第二因緣。由此煩惱斷他善品，授不善品，是第三因緣。除先所作能往惡趣順後受業。又十煩惱，七唯意地，貪、恚、無明亦通五識。
items.en: Desire-realm afflictions, serving as the foundation for unwholesome conduct, are mostly unwholesome. Unwholesome afflictions possessing three conditions definitely lead to a miserable rebirth; other afflictions do not necessarily do so. What are the three? Extensive, earnest, uninterrupted cultivation, mistaken for merit, its fault and harm unseen, indulged without restraint — this is the first condition. Relying on this affliction as a basis for committing and increasing unwholesome deeds through body, speech, and mind — this is the second. Using this affliction to sever another's wholesome roots and instil unwholesome ones — this is the third. This excludes karma from a past life whose result is delayed to a later rebirth. Also, of the ten afflictions, seven belong only to the mind ground; greed, hatred, and ignorance also extend to the five sense-consciousnesses.

items.title: Section: Which Feelings Accompany Which Affliction, and What Each One Actually Latches Onto

items.zh: 又於欲界，四見及慢，喜、捨相應；貪，樂、喜捨相應；恚，苦、憂、捨相應；邪見，喜、憂、捨相應；疑，憂、捨相應；無明，一切五根相應。此據多分相應道理，其餘深細，後當廣說。於上諸地隨所有根，即與彼地煩惱相應。又十煩惱，見所斷者，名曰無事，彼所緣事非成實故。所餘煩惱有事，無事彼相違故。又貪與慢緣有漏一分可意事生，恚緣一分非可意生，是故此三煩惱一分所生，名取一分。所餘煩惱，通緣內外若愛非愛，及俱相違有漏事生，是故說彼名曰遍行，取一切事。
items.en: In the desire realm, four views and conceit are accompanied by joy and equanimity; greed by pleasure, joy, and equanimity; hatred by pain, sorrow, and equanimity; wrong view by joy, sorrow, and equanimity; doubt by sorrow and equanimity; ignorance by all five. Afflictions severed by the path of vision are called "without real basis," since the thing they take as object is never conventionally real. Greed and conceit arise in relation to a partial, desirable outflow-bound object; hatred arises in relation to a partial, undesirable one — these three are said to take a partial object. The remaining afflictions, ranging across internal and external, desirable, undesirable, and neither, are called pervasive, taking every object as their scope.

items.title: Section: A New Topic Opens — What Are the Secondary Afflictions?

items.zh: 若有隨順如是煩惱、煩惱俱行、煩惱品類，名隨煩惱。云何名隨煩惱？略由四相差別建立。一、通一切不善心起；二、通一切染污心起；三、於各別不善心起；四、善、不善、無記心起，非一切處、非一切時。
items.en: Whatever accords with these afflictions, arises together with them, or belongs to their category, is called secondary affliction. What is secondary affliction? It is established, in brief, through four distinguishing aspects: pervading every unwholesome mind; pervading every defiled mind; arising with a specific unwholesome mind; and arising with wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral minds, though not in every place or at every time.

items.title: Section: Shamelessness, Ten Great Afflictions, and Ten That Never Arise Together

items.zh: 謂無慚無愧，名通一切不善心起。隨煩惱放逸、掉舉、惛沈、不信、懈怠、邪欲、邪勝解、邪念、散亂、不正知，此十隨煩惱，通一切染污心起。通一切處三界所繫。忿、恨、覆、惱、嫉、慳、誑、諂、憍、害，此十隨煩惱，各別不善心起。若一生時，必無第二。如是十種，皆欲界繫，除誑、諂、憍。由誑及諂至初靜慮。憍通三界，此并前二，若在上地，唯無記性。
items.en: Shamelessness and lack of regard for others pervade every unwholesome mind. Heedlessness, restlessness, dullness, lack of faith, laziness, wrong desire, wrong conviction, wrong mindfulness, distraction, and incorrect discernment — these ten pervade every defiled mind, confined to no single realm. Wrath, resentment, concealment, vexation, envy, stinginess, deceit, flattery, arrogance, and the wish to harm — these ten arise individually with a specific unwholesome mind; when one arises, none of the others can arise alongside it. All ten are confined to the desire realm, except deceit, flattery, and arrogance. Deceit and flattery extend as far as the first absorption. Arrogance extends across all three realms; together with the previous two, in the higher realms it becomes purely neutral.

items.title: Section: A Monk's Cure for a Dying Man — Three Kinds of Delusive Thought

items.zh: 尋、伺、惡作、睡眠，此四隨煩惱，通善、不善、無記心起，非一切處、非一切時。若有極久尋求伺察，便令身疲、念失，心亦勞損，是故尋、伺名隨煩惱。此二乃至初靜慮地。惡作、睡眠唯在欲界。又有定地諸隨煩惱。謂尋、伺、誑、諂、惛沈、掉舉、憍、放逸、懈怠等。初靜慮地有初四種，餘通一切地。若雜事中，世尊所說諸隨煩惱，廣說乃至愁、歎、憂、苦隨擾惱等，及攝事分廣所分別，如是一切諸隨煩惱，皆是此中四相差別，隨其所應，相攝應知。
items.en: Examination, reflection, regret, and drowsiness — these four arise across wholesome, unwholesome, and neutral minds, though not universally nor at every time. Prolonged examination and reflection tire the body, cause loss of mindfulness, and strain the mind, which is why they are called secondary afflictions; these two extend as far as the first absorption. Regret and drowsiness belong only to the desire realm. All the varieties of secondary affliction the Blessed One spoke of elsewhere, extending to grief, lamentation, sorrow, and distress, and all that is analysed at length in the Compendium of Bases, are without exception subsumed under these same four categories, according to what applies.

items.zh: 復次，諸隨煩惱，若在欲界，略於十二處轉。何等十二？

items.title: Section: Twelve Situations Where Affliction Takes Root, and the Monk Who Hid His Own Excrement

items.zh: 謂執著惡行處；鬪訟諍競處；毀犯尸羅處；受學隨轉非善人法處；邪命處；耽著諸欲處；如所聞法義，心諦思惟處；於所思義，內心寂止方便持心處；展轉受用財法處；不相雜住處；遠離臥具房舍處；眾苦所集處。此十二處以為依止，如先所說貪著，乃至隨擾惱等諸隨煩惱，差別而轉。謂貪著、瞋恚、愚癡，依初處轉；忿等乃至諂，依第二處轉；
items.en: Clinging to bad conduct; quarreling and contention; breaking ethical discipline; following the unwholesome ways of a bad teacher; wrong livelihood; indulging in desire; reflecting carefully on a teaching just heard; stilling the mind through meditative practice on its meaning; mutually sharing wealth and teaching; living incompatibly among fellow practitioners; dwelling apart in solitary lodging; and the gathering-place of every suffering. Greed, hatred, and delusion arise from the first situation; wrath through flattery arise from the second.

blocks.text: How afflictions relate to the realms and to feelings, and the twenty "secondary" afflictions that follow the root ones.
Master Cháng Bǎi: desire-realm beings can think about the higher realms' afflictions only as names. Adopted self-view, firmly held, obstructs the noble path even above.

Three conditions. Master Cháng Bǎi: not seeing the affliction's fault, one lets the mind run; by it one severs others' wholesome roots and teaches them to do likewise. The exception is karma from earlier lives that leads to lower rebirth on its own.
Master Cháng Bǎi: view-afflictions are mostly confusions about principle; "with a basis" means a real object, like craving food when hungry.
Master Cháng Bǎi: what acts with affliction and arises in its wake is "secondary".
Master Cháng Bǎi: shamelessness and the like pervade the unwholesome; wrath and the other nine are coarse and arise one at a time. Deceit and flattery usually involve fame and gain.
Master Cháng Bǎi: excessive thinking about desires, doctrine, or worldly affairs tires body and mind and obstructs calm and insight.
Master Cháng Bǎi: clinging to bad conduct gives rise to greed, hatred, and delusion; in fights and quarrels, wrath and resentment.
Even thinking about the Dharma, done obsessively, is listed among delusive thoughts. Too much thinking blocks calm and insight.

quiz.q: How does the lecture qualify "lower afflictions take higher ones"?
options: desire-realm beings directly perceive higher realms, as with the divine eye
only those with absorption can take higher realms
lower afflictions cannot take higher ones at all
not directly: they take only names, and what names denote, arisen from discrimination
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: desire-realm beings can reach up to the afflictions and contaminated matters of the form and formless realms, yet only as names and what names denote, as arisen in the discriminating mind. The English needs that qualification to avoid implying direct access.

quiz.q: How do innate and adopted self-view differ in moral quality?
options: innate is purely unwholesome, being hardest to sever; adopted is neutral throughout, being mere ideas harming no one, unrelated to the control of absorption
both are purely wholesome
both are purely unwholesome
innate is purely neutral; adopted is unwholesome in desire, and a concealed neutral above
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: adopted self-view, firmly held, differs from the innate neutral kind; the power of calm-abiding controls it above, yet with defiled wisdom as essence it obstructs the noble path and is concealed. The English "a concealed kind of neutrality" is good for 隱沒.

quiz.q: Which three conditions make an unwholesome affliction lead to a miserable rebirth?
options: much practice taken as merit; committing and increasing evil through it; severing others' good and instilling bad
birth in a borderland, bad friends, and not hearing the Dharma
greed, hatred, and delusion being present
those severed by vision, cultivation, and adepts
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: not seeing the affliction's fault, one lets the mind run unchecked; by such affliction one severs others' wholesome roots and further teaches them to act so. The treatise then excepts prior later-life karma able to lead to evil destinies.

quiz.q: The English has "karma from a past life whose result is delayed to a later rebirth." What is left out?
options: it omits 能往惡趣: only such karma leading to evil destinies is excepted, and the English is too broad
nothing: all later-life karma leads to evil destinies anyway, the phrase being redundant, as the lecture says none of it leads to good destinies
it omits 順後
it omits 先所作
quiz.why: The exception is only prior later-life karma that leads to evil destinies, since such karma might bring a fall even without the three conditions. The English drops the qualifier, making all later-life karma excepted. Master Cháng Bǎi's account of the second condition, doing and increasing evil, fits the main clause.

quiz.q: The English has "lack genuine substance." What is wrong with the subject?
options: 無事 concerns the object, not conventionally real; the English says the afflictions themselves lack substance
no problem: such afflictions themselves have no substance and leave no trace once severed
the problem is "vision," which should be "sight"
the problem is "path," which should be "road"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: these are mostly conceptual confusions about principle; by contrast, what has a basis means an object conventionally real, such as craving food when hungry. So 無事 describes the object. The English "lack genuine substance" moves it onto the afflictions, though its next clause mentions the object.

quiz.q: What are "taking a partial object" and "pervasive"?
options: greed, conceit, and hatred take a part; the others range over all
severed-by-vision afflictions are partial, taking part of the truths; severed-by-cultivation afflictions are pervasive, running with the aggregates, whatever their kind
greed, hatred, delusion are partial; views, conceit, doubt pervasive
higher afflictions are partial; desire-realm ones pervasive
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: these three arise from a portion of circumstances and take a part as object; the others range over the inner body and outer objects, lovely, unlovely, or neither. The English "partial object" and "pervasive" fit.

quiz.q: What is a secondary affliction, and what is the defiled mind in "pervading every defiled mind"?
options: afflictions lighter than the root ones, independent of them
what accords with, arises with, or belongs to root afflictions; defiled mind means concealed-neutral mind
afflictions only of outsiders; defiled mind means greed
afflictions after vision; defiled mind means wholesome mind
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: what acts together with affliction and belongs to the ten's classes, arising in their wake, is secondary affliction; and the second aspect arises only with defiled mind, meaning concealed-neutral mind. So the second aspect is broader than the first, reaching beyond unwholesome mind.

quiz.q: To which aspect do shamelessness, the ten of heedlessness, and the ten of wrath belong?
options: pervading defiled mind; individual; pervading unwholesome mind, shamelessness being heaviest and reaching all defilement, wrath and the like being in every unwholesome mind
reaching all three natures; unwholesome; defiled
all arise individually
pervading unwholesome mind; pervading defiled mind; arising individually
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: shamelessness and the like arise together and pervade the unwholesome only, not the concealed kind; the ten of wrath are coarse and fierce, arising individually, each as chief. The English says "lack of regard for others" for 無愧, a workable rendering.

quiz.q: How far do deceit, flattery, and arrogance extend, and what is their quality above?
options: all three stay in the desire realm, and are unwholesome above
deceit and flattery reach the first absorption, tied to fame and gain; arrogance reaches all three; above they are neutral, under calm-abiding, yet obstruct the path
all three reach all realms, unwholesome above
deceit and flattery all three; arrogance the first; wholesome above
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: deceit and flattery usually involve fame and gain, and so reach only the first absorption; subdued by calm-abiding they are neutral, yet they obstruct the noble path. Another passage in the lecture misstates this; the treatise wording settles it.

quiz.q: Why are examination and reflection called secondary afflictions?
options: since they are in essence greed, hatred, and delusion
they arise only in the higher realms
they are the seeds of the three poisons
prolonged use tires the body, loses mindfulness, and strains the mind, obstructing calm and insight
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the body tires, mindfulness is lost, and the mind is strained; excessive thinking about desires, doctrine, or worldly affairs harms body and mind and obstructs calm and insight. So the problem is excess; the treatise says these reach all three natures.

quiz.q: How far do examination, reflection, regret, and drowsiness extend, and why not regret above?
options: examination and reflection only in desire; regret and drowsiness to the first absorption, first-absorption gods sleeping and regretting while thought has stopped
all four reach all three realms
examination and reflection to the first absorption; regret and drowsiness only in desire, higher beings lacking regret
all four are only of the desire realm
quiz.why: The treatise says examination and reflection reach the first absorption, and regret and drowsiness stay in the desire realm. Master Cháng Bǎi: beings of the upper two realms have no such remorse. All four reach wholesome, unwholesome, and neutral minds. The English is accurate.

quiz.q: Which afflictions arise from the first and second of the twelve situations?
options: breaking discipline: the three; wrong livelihood: wrath through flattery
wrong livelihood: shamelessness; indulgence: deceit
clinging to bad conduct: greed, hatred, delusion; quarreling: wrath through flattery
the gathering of suffering: greed; solitude: hatred
quiz.why: The treatise matches these in order. Master Cháng Bǎi: clinging to bad conduct of body, speech, and mind gives rise to greed, hatred, and delusion; in fights and quarrels, wrath, resentment, concealment, vexation, envy, stinginess, deceit, and flattery appear. The twelve show where affliction takes hold.
